incident_summary: SYNTHETIC rehearsal only. A corporate enquiry received on 15 September requested 18 rooms for 36 people over two November nights, meeting facilities, coffee breaks and a wine gala dinner, near a USD 10,000 budget. Room configuration, dinner arrangements and payment terms differed from the request. The respondent reports that two conditional proposals preceded a USD 10,296 gross authorized offer sent at 14:00 on 17 September, four hours after the client's deadline. A supplied fictional client email reports choosing another venue at 11:40, citing missing final terms and preferable dinner space and payment terms. Conversion with an earlier offer is unknown. No incremental cash expenditure was recorded; staff effort was not measured.

handover_failure_mechanism.summary: SYNTHETIC analyst reconstruction: Sales acknowledged ownership and the deadline; F&B recorded service constraints; V1 remained conditional on staffing and a deposit exception. The respondent reports that an authorized package was not issued by the client deadline. The missing Sales-to-F&B request, contemporaneous package worksheet, second proposal and approval records prevent identifying a specific failed transfer, missed acknowledgement or responsible decision timestamp. Multiple dependent commercial decisions are established, but a precise handover failure and its causal contribution relative to venue and payment fit remain unresolved.

alternative_explanations: The client explicitly preferred the competing venue's private dinner room and payment schedule; an earlier offer on the hotel's eventual terms might still have been rejected.
An existing restaurant commitment and cellar capacity constrained service fit. The proposed alternative changed privacy, wines, tasting groups and dinner timing.
The requested 10% deposit and post-event balance required an owner exception. The decision history and final approved payment terms were not supplied.
The available 14 twins plus four doubles differed from the requested 18 twins; its effect on the outcome is unknown.
The reported USD 10,296 gross final package exceeded the stated USD 10,000 budget; the client did not explicitly identify that price difference as a rejection reason.
Potential transient displacement was forecast rather than reserved demand. The estimates do not establish actual displaced bookings or losses.
The comparator had fewer rooms, different dates, no restaurant conflict and no owner-level payment exception, so it does not isolate response speed or worksheet effectiveness.
Missing request, worksheet-version and approval records leave the precise cause of unresolved terms unknown.

a2a_suitability.simple_rule_inadequacy_rationale: Ordinary worksheet use and one late offer do not demonstrate that a clearer checkpoint or approval rule is inadequate. The respondent proposed tightening the existing process; no benchmark established superiority of a more complex approach.

real_problem.recency_rationale: Within the fictional account, the 15–17 September enquiry occurred six to eight days before the 23 September interview, and no completed subsequent process change was reported. This does not satisfy a real-world evidence gate because the entire case is synthetic.
real_problem.consequence: Within the rehearsal, the respondent confirms a missed opportunity after firm terms were reportedly sent late. The client email also identifies competing venue advantages; guaranteed conversion is not established.

materiality.rationale: The respondent called this a missed opportunity and said 18 rooms affects most of the 24-room hotel, but did not establish measured serious loss or materiality relative to other problems. The ledger supports zero actual cash leakage; labor effort and opportunity value remain unmeasured.

software_leverage.available_information: Supplied fictional excerpts contain an acknowledged client deadline, inventory estimates, service constraints and V1 conditional terms. Complete approval history, contemporaneous worksheet state and final payment terms are unavailable.

simple_rule.baseline_description: Respondent describes ordinary use of a shared worksheet recording response owner, client deadline, rate limits, menu version, deposit terms and approval exceptions. An earlier decision checkpoint was proposed but not implemented or benchmarked.

severity.rationale: Reviewer assessment of the fictional account: a client chose elsewhere and the respondent identified a missed opportunity, but actual cash leakage was zero and neither labor cost nor lost contribution was measured. Serious or recurring harm is not established.

a2a_fit.rationale: Reviewer assessment of the fictional account: service confirmation and commercial review affected the Sales response across several responsibilities. Exact failed handoffs and a need beyond explicit rules or ordinary approval controls remain unproven.

feasibility.rationale: No engineering estimate, integration, permitted writes, replay cases, deterministic oracle or recovery test was supplied.

evidence.rationale: Assessment only of rehearsal evidence completeness: several fictional excerpts support parts of the incident and a signed-booking comparator, but key versions, approvals, a valid denominator and independent responsibility accounts are missing. This rating establishes no real-world evidence.

frequency.rationale: Only one affected enquiry is identified. The described 12-enquiry register lacks client deadlines and was not supplied, so neither recurrence nor a 30-day-equivalent missed-deadline rate is established.

preventable_share.rationale: No permitted intervention or quantified preventable loss was established. Client preferences and substantive service/payment constraints prevent attributing the opportunity entirely to response timing.

adoption.rationale: The respondent made a dated rehearsal commitment to draft an existing-process revision. This supports limited process-change intent, not adoption of technology, colleague agreement, trial authorization or completed implementation.
